newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick posts improved first half despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick posts improved first half despite strong pound.

text.p: Improved performance in the United States contributed to an increase in first-half profits by British insurance broker Sedgwick Group despite continuing weak insurance rates and the adverse impact of the pound, the company said Tuesday.
Pretax profits rose to 66.5 million pounds ($104.9 million) over the six months from 64.1 million pounds ($101.1 million) a year earlier.
Excluding the effect of the currency, which took 7 million pounds ($11 million) from earnings, profits were up 16 percent over the period.
For the year as a whole, the company expects the pound to take just under 9 million pounds ($14 million) off profits.
Stocks gave a muted response to the figures, which were broadly in line with analyst forecasts, adding 1 pence ($1.58) to 120 pence ($1.892).
Chairman Sax Riley described the performance as encouraging and said the company's strategy of expanding the range of services offered to clients through its worldwide network was continuing.
He once again hinted that Sedgwick would not rule out the possibility of a merger with British rival Willis Corroon Group Plc.
Sedgwick had made it clear that it wanted to grow and increase revenues, said Riley.
"You have to compare what we have said and what (Willis Chairman) John Reeve has said and draw your own conclusions," he said.
Some analysts suggest a tie-up with Willis could provide the two companies with a solution to the problems posed by the intense competition and slim margins.
They argue something dramatic is needed to close the gap with U.S. rivals Aon Corp. and Marsh & Mclennan Cos. Inc.

Sedgwick said it aimed to continue with small, add-on purchases, particularly in continental Europe as long as they provided shareholder value and gave Sedgwick management and dividend policy control.
